title: Thyroid Cancer
subtitle: StewardMD ONCOTREE navigator (draft)
provenanceNote: ONCOTREE navigator DRAFT for thyroid cancer authored from standard references (NCCN/DeVita/Harrison) - the physician decides. Full pathway by histologic subtype (differentiated, medullary, anaplastic, previously-treated surveillance), then subtype-specific workup and staging / risk stratification (tables) -> definitive surgery -> a radioiodine-adjuvant decision -> a dynamic-response restaging question -> surveillance, with advanced / radioiodine-refractory and RET / BRAF / NTRK molecular arms each refined through a line-of-therapy sub-tree (first line -> on progression -> next line). Recurrence and structural-incomplete responses re-enter the advanced pathway. Treatment leaves route to APPLICABLE existing StewardMD Standard Protocols by reference; agents without a dose protocol here (radioiodine, TSH-suppressive levothyroxine, lenvatinib / sorafenib, larotrectinib / entrectinib, cabozantinib / vandetanib, cytotoxic chemoradiation) are shown as checklist guidance with NO dose. matchDisease:false because the subtypes carry different protocol diseaseId tags. Invents no dose / regimen / criterion. Structural pathway consistent with Standard Guidelines (NCCN) Thyroid Carcinoma; no proprietary content reproduced. DRAFT - not clinically activated; the physician decides and the existing dose engine computes patient doses.
sourceNote: Structural pathway consistent with Standard Guidelines (NCCN / DeVita / Harrison), Thyroid Carcinoma. Regimen options reference existing StewardMD Standard Protocols and their own evidence layers; the dose engine computes patient doses.

a.text: Post-operative recurrence-risk category (low / intermediate / high) is estimated from tumor size, extrathyroidal extension, resection completeness, vascular invasion, aggressive histology, nodal burden and post-op thyroglobulin. It drives extent of surgery, whether radioiodine is given, and the initial TSH target. Reassess it dynamically at each follow-up.

b.text: Radioiodine (I-131) is used for remnant ablation, adjuvant treatment of residual microscopic disease, or therapy of iodine-avid metastases. It requires TSH stimulation (thyroid-hormone withdrawal or recombinant human TSH) and a low-iodine diet. Confirm iodine avidity on a diagnostic or post-therapy scan before relying on it in metastatic disease.

c.text: Selective RET inhibitors (selpercatinib, pralsetinib) are preferred for RET-mutant medullary and RET-fusion-positive differentiated thyroid cancer, with high response rates and better tolerability than multikinase inhibitors. Confirm the RET alteration on validated tissue or plasma NGS before treating.

d.text: Anaplastic thyroid carcinoma is an oncologic emergency: secure the airway, obtain rapid BRAF V600E testing, and start systemic therapy without delay. BRAF V600E-mutant disease responds to dabrafenib plus trametinib (with consideration of subsequent surgery / an immune-checkpoint inhibitor); BRAF wild-type disease is driven by any other actionable alteration or managed on trial / with cytotoxic chemoradiation.

e.text: Dynamic response to therapy (excellent / indeterminate / biochemically-incomplete / structurally-incomplete) is reassessed at each visit from thyroglobulin (or calcitonin / CEA for medullary), antibody status, and imaging. It re-sets the TSH target and decides whether to observe, re-treat locally, or re-enter the advanced systemic pathway.

nodes.name: Initial workup
nodes.title: Initial workup and diagnosis
nodes.description: Baseline evaluation of a thyroid nodule or biopsy-proven thyroid cancer before subtype-directed management.
bullets: History and neck exam: compressive / voice symptoms, prior neck irradiation, family history of thyroid cancer or MEN2
Serum TSH; neck ultrasound of the thyroid and central + lateral compartments
FNA of the nodule with a Bethesda cytology category; molecular testing (e.g. Afirma / ThyroSeq) for indeterminate Bethesda III-IV
Serum calcitonin and CEA if medullary carcinoma is suspected or before thyroid surgery per local practice
Cross-sectional imaging (contrast CT neck / chest) and laryngoscopy for bulky, fixed, substernal, or clinically aggressive disease; confirm the histologic subtype - it determines the entire pathway

nodes.name: Histology / subtype
nodes.title: Histologic subtype
nodes.description: Thyroid cancer subtype defines a distinct pathway. Choose the confirmed histology, or enter surveillance for a previously treated patient.

nodes.name: DTC staging workup
nodes.title: Differentiated: staging and molecular workup
nodes.description: Complete subtype-specific staging before assigning a recurrence-risk category.
bullets: Document AJCC TNM stage using age at diagnosis (age < 55 vs >= 55 markedly changes stage)
Neck ultrasound mapping of nodal compartments before surgery
Aggressive histology on path? tall-cell, hobnail, columnar, diffuse-sclerosing papillary, or widely-invasive / poorly-differentiated follicular raises risk
Molecular profiling of advanced or radioiodine-refractory disease (BRAF, RAS, NTRK and RET fusions, TERT promoter) identifies targeted-therapy candidates
Baseline post-op thyroglobulin and anti-thyroglobulin antibody once healed

nodes.name: DTC risk / stage
nodes.title: Differentiated: recurrence-risk category
nodes.description: Assign a post-operative recurrence-risk category (or select advanced / metastatic or recurrent disease). Risk drives extent of surgery, radioiodine use, and TSH target.

tables.title: Differentiated thyroid cancer - recurrence-risk category (illustrative)
rows: Intrathyroidal papillary <= 4 cm, N0 / Nx or <= 5 micro-nodes, no aggressive histology or vascular invasion
Lobectomy or total thyroidectomy; radioiodine usually not needed; TSH low-normal
Microscopic extrathyroidal extension, aggressive histology, vascular invasion, or clinical N1
Total thyroidectomy; consider adjuvant radioiodine; mild TSH suppression
Gross extrathyroidal extension, incomplete resection, distant metastases, or high post-op thyroglobulin
Total thyroidectomy + therapeutic neck dissection; radioiodine; TSH suppression < 0.1

options.label: Papillary microcarcinoma (<= 1 cm, no adverse features)

nodes.name: Micropapillary
nodes.title: Papillary microcarcinoma: active surveillance or lobectomy
nodes.description: Very-low-risk papillary microcarcinoma; observation is a validated alternative to immediate surgery.
bullets: Active surveillance with serial ultrasound is appropriate for selected patients without nodal disease, extrathyroidal extension, or high-risk cytology
Lobectomy if the tumor grows, develops adverse features, or the patient prefers surgery
No radioiodine; keep TSH low-normal
Not suitable when the tumor abuts the trachea / recurrent laryngeal nerve or shows aggressive histology
Enter differentiated-cancer surveillance

nodes.name: DTC low risk
nodes.title: Low-risk DTC: surgery, selective radioiodine
nodes.description: Surgery is definitive for most low-risk disease; radioiodine is generally not required. Proceed to the adjuvant-radioiodine decision.
bullets: Lobectomy for a unifocal intrathyroidal tumor <= 4 cm; total thyroidectomy if bilateral disease, patient preference, or to enable radioiodine / thyroglobulin monitoring
Levothyroxine to keep TSH low-normal (about 0.5 to 2.0 mIU/L) after lobectomy
Radioiodine usually omitted - confirm at the adjuvant-radioiodine decision (next step)
Then move to dynamic-response restaging

nodes.name: DTC intermediate risk
nodes.title: Intermediate-risk DTC: total thyroidectomy, risk-adapted radioiodine
nodes.description: Total thyroidectomy with risk-adapted radioiodine and modest TSH suppression. Proceed to the adjuvant-radioiodine decision.
bullets: Total thyroidectomy; therapeutic central / lateral neck dissection for proven nodal disease
TSH suppression to about 0.1 to 0.5 mIU/L, relaxed over time with an excellent response
Adjuvant radioiodine is considered but not automatic - decide at the next step
Then move to dynamic-response restaging

nodes.name: DTC high risk
nodes.title: High-risk (M0) DTC: total thyroidectomy, radioiodine, deep TSH suppression
nodes.description: Aggressive locoregional disease without distant metastases. Proceed to the adjuvant-radioiodine decision.
bullets: Total thyroidectomy with therapeutic compartmental neck dissection; resect gross extrathyroidal disease where feasible
External-beam radiation for unresectable or recurrent locoregional disease not controlled by surgery / radioiodine
TSH suppression < 0.1 mIU/L while disease persists, balanced against cardiac / skeletal risk
Adjuvant radioiodine is expected - confirm at the next step, then move to dynamic-response restaging

nodes.name: Adjuvant RAI decision
nodes.title: Differentiated: adjuvant radioiodine decision
nodes.description: After total thyroidectomy, decide whether adjuvant radioiodine is given. Choice is risk-adapted and requires TSH stimulation and a low-iodine diet.
bullets: Low-risk, node-negative disease after total thyroidectomy: radioiodine usually omitted
Intermediate-risk: individualized adjuvant activity for higher-risk features
High-risk / gross residual: adjuvant radioiodine is expected; nuclear medicine sets the activity (no dose protocol here)

nodes.name: DTC dynamic response
nodes.title: Differentiated: dynamic response restaging
nodes.description: Reassess response 6-12 months after definitive therapy from thyroglobulin (with antibody status) and imaging. The response category re-sets the TSH target and the next step.

tables.title: Differentiated thyroid cancer - dynamic response categories
rows: Nonspecific findings, low-level stable thyroglobulin or antibodies
Continue mild suppression; re-image at interval
Rising / detectable thyroglobulin, no structural correlate
Maintain suppression; additional imaging or empiric radioiodine in selected cases
Restage; local therapy or the advanced systemic pathway

nodes.name: DTC biochemical-incomplete
nodes.title: Biochemically-incomplete response: suppress and re-image
nodes.description: Detectable / rising thyroglobulin without a structural correlate.
bullets: Maintain TSH suppression; trend thyroglobulin and anti-thyroglobulin antibody for a doubling-time
Neck ultrasound and cross-sectional imaging to find a structural source before escalating
Rising thyroglobulin with negative imaging: consider a diagnostic radioiodine scan or FDG-PET (dedifferentiation)
Empiric radioiodine only in selected iodine-avid cases; otherwise observe
Continue differentiated-cancer surveillance

nodes.name: DTC restage
nodes.title: Structurally-incomplete response: restage
nodes.description: Structural disease is present. Distinguish resectable locoregional disease from distant metastases, which decides local versus systemic therapy.
bullets: Cross-sectional imaging (CT neck / chest) and a diagnostic radioiodine scan to map disease and iodine avidity
Resectable neck disease: compartment-oriented reoperation
Distant metastases: enter the radioiodine-avidity pathway

nodes.name: DTC locoregional recurrence
nodes.title: Locoregional recurrence: compartmental reoperation
nodes.description: Resectable locoregional recurrence without distant metastases.
bullets: Compartment-oriented therapeutic neck dissection of biopsy-proven recurrence (avoid repeated berry-picking)
Radioiodine if the recurrence is iodine-avid and not fully resected
External-beam radiation for unresectable or repeatedly recurrent disease
Consider active surveillance for small-volume, stable, non-threatening nodal disease
Re-enter surveillance; move to the advanced pathway if distant metastases appear

nodes.name: RAI status
nodes.title: Advanced DTC: radioiodine avidity
nodes.description: Distant metastatic differentiated disease is managed first by whether it concentrates radioiodine. Confirm avidity on a scan before relying on it.
bullets: Iodine-avid metastases can respond durably to repeated radioiodine
Radioiodine-refractory = no iodine uptake, progression despite uptake, or progression within about 12 months of a therapeutic dose

nodes.name: RAI-avid metastatic
nodes.title: RAI-avid metastatic DTC: radioiodine therapy
nodes.description: Iodine-avid distant metastases treated with therapeutic radioiodine and TSH suppression; re-evaluate at progression.
bullets: Therapeutic radioiodine after TSH stimulation and a low-iodine diet; repeat while disease remains avid and responding
TSH suppression < 0.1 mIU/L between treatments
Directed local therapy (surgery, external-beam radiation, or ablation) for symptomatic, dominant, or CNS / weight-bearing bone lesions; add a bone-modifying agent for skeletal metastases
On loss of avidity or progression within about 12 months: enter the radioiodine-refractory biomarker pathway

nodes.name: Refractory biomarker
nodes.title: RAI-refractory DTC: actionable biomarker (first line)
nodes.description: In radioiodine-refractory progressive disease, a driver alteration changes first-line therapy from a multikinase inhibitor to a selective targeted agent.

tables.title: Actionable drivers in radioiodine-refractory DTC
rows: BRAF-directed therapy (e.g. dabrafenib +/- trametinib; redifferentiation strategies in trials)

nodes.name: NTRK fusion DTC 1L
nodes.title: RAI-refractory, NTRK fusion: TRK inhibitor (first line)
nodes.description: NTRK-fusion-positive radioiodine-refractory differentiated thyroid cancer, first line.
bullets: Larotrectinib or entrectinib (tissue-agnostic TRK inhibitor indication) - high, durable response rates
Confirm the NTRK fusion on validated NGS
Referenced dose protocol below (larotrectinib; entrectinib is an alternative)
Continue TSH suppression; monitor for the disease response and for acquired resistance
On progression: reassess for a next-line option

nodes.name: TRK progression
nodes.title: NTRK-fusion DTC: on progression
nodes.description: Progression on a first-generation TRK inhibitor. Distinguish limited (oligoprogressive) disease from systemic progression.

nodes.name: NTRK fusion DTC 2L
nodes.title: NTRK-fusion DTC: next-generation TRK inhibitor / MKI
nodes.description: Systemic progression on a first-generation TRK inhibitor.
bullets: Re-biopsy / plasma NGS to identify an on-target resistance kinase-domain mutation (e.g. solvent-front)
A next-generation TRK inhibitor (e.g. selitrectinib / repotrectinib, trial or off-label) for an on-target mechanism
Otherwise switch to a multikinase inhibitor (lenvatinib) as for driver-negative disease
Referenced dose protocol below is the lenvatinib multikinase-inhibitor option
Continue TSH suppression; re-enter surveillance

nodes.name: RET fusion DTC 1L
nodes.title: RAI-refractory, RET fusion: selective RET inhibitor (first line)
nodes.description: RET-fusion-positive radioiodine-refractory differentiated thyroid cancer, first line.
bullets: Selpercatinib (or pralsetinib) - selective RET inhibitor, preferred over multikinase inhibitors
Confirm the RET fusion on validated tissue or plasma NGS
Referenced dose protocol is the medullary-scoped selpercatinib protocol (same drug); the physician confirms the fit
Continue TSH suppression; monitor LFTs, blood pressure, QT, and hypersensitivity
On progression: reassess for a next-line option

nodes.name: RET progression DTC
nodes.title: RET-fusion DTC: on progression
nodes.description: Progression on a selective RET inhibitor. Distinguish oligoprogressive from systemic progression.

nodes.name: RET fusion DTC 2L
nodes.title: RET-fusion DTC: multikinase inhibitor after a RET inhibitor
nodes.description: Systemic progression on a selective RET inhibitor.
bullets: Re-biopsy / plasma NGS for an acquired RET resistance mutation (e.g. solvent-front G810) or a bypass driver
Lenvatinib (or sorafenib / cabozantinib) multikinase inhibitor as the next line
A next-generation RET inhibitor on trial for an on-target solvent-front mutation where available
Referenced dose protocol below is the lenvatinib multikinase-inhibitor option
Continue TSH suppression; re-enter surveillance

nodes.name: BRAF DTC 1L
nodes.title: RAI-refractory, BRAF V600E: BRAF-directed therapy (first line)
nodes.description: BRAF V600E-positive radioiodine-refractory differentiated thyroid cancer.
bullets: BRAF-directed therapy (dabrafenib +/- trametinib) for progressive BRAF V600E-mutant disease
Redifferentiation with a BRAF / MEK inhibitor to restore iodine avidity is an investigational strategy in selected patients
Lenvatinib remains an accepted first-line multikinase option if BRAF-directed therapy is not chosen
Referenced dose protocol is the anaplastic-scoped dabrafenib + trametinib protocol (same drugs / doses); the physician confirms the fit
Continue TSH suppression; reassess at progression

nodes.name: BRAF progression DTC
nodes.title: BRAF V600E DTC: on progression
nodes.description: Progression on BRAF-directed therapy. Distinguish oligoprogressive from systemic progression.

nodes.name: BRAF DTC 2L
nodes.title: BRAF V600E DTC: multikinase inhibitor after BRAF-directed therapy
nodes.description: Systemic progression on BRAF-directed therapy.
bullets: Switch to a multikinase inhibitor (lenvatinib, then sorafenib or cabozantinib) as for driver-negative disease
Reassess NGS for a new actionable alteration or dedifferentiation to anaplastic transformation
Directed local therapy for dominant or symptomatic lesions
Referenced dose protocol below is the lenvatinib multikinase-inhibitor option
Continue TSH suppression; re-enter surveillance

nodes.name: RAI-refractory MKI 1L
nodes.title: RAI-refractory, no target: lenvatinib / sorafenib (first line)
nodes.description: Progressive radioiodine-refractory disease without an actionable driver.
bullets: Lenvatinib is the preferred multikinase inhibitor (higher response rate); sorafenib is an alternative
Reserve systemic therapy for progressive or symptomatic disease - indolent metastases can be observed
Referenced dose protocol below is lenvatinib; manage hypertension, proteinuria, diarrhea, hand-foot skin reaction, and thromboembolic / bleeding risk
Continue TSH suppression; use directed local therapy for dominant lesions
On progression: reassess for a next-line multikinase inhibitor

nodes.name: MKI progression DTC
nodes.title: RAI-refractory MKI: on progression
nodes.description: Progression on first-line lenvatinib / sorafenib. Distinguish oligoprogressive from systemic progression.

nodes.name: RAI-refractory MKI 2L
nodes.title: RAI-refractory, no target: second-line multikinase inhibitor / trial
nodes.description: Systemic progression on first-line lenvatinib / sorafenib.
bullets: Cabozantinib is an accepted option after progression on prior VEGFR-directed multikinase therapy
Sorafenib or lenvatinib if not already used; re-send NGS to catch a late actionable driver
Clinical trial or best supportive care per performance status and goals
Referenced dose protocol below is cabozantinib
Continue TSH suppression; re-enter surveillance

nodes.name: DTC surveillance
nodes.title: Differentiated: surveillance and recurrence check
nodes.description: Longitudinal monitoring after therapy; a rising thyroglobulin or new structural disease reopens the response / advanced pathway.
bullets: Serum thyroglobulin + anti-thyroglobulin antibody and neck ultrasound at intervals; assign a dynamic response category
Adjust the TSH target upward as the response becomes excellent; deepen suppression if disease persists
Rising thyroglobulin with negative imaging: consider a diagnostic radioiodine scan or FDG-PET (dedifferentiation)
Structural recurrence: surgery or directed local therapy for resectable disease; enter the advanced / radioiodine pathway for distant metastases
Monitor for over-suppression effects (atrial fibrillation, bone loss)

nodes.name: MTC workup
nodes.title: Medullary: workup and RET testing
nodes.description: Medullary carcinoma arises from calcitonin-producing C-cells and is RET-driven. Complete germline and biochemical workup before surgery.

tables.title: Medullary carcinoma - RET germline context (MEN2)
rows: Screen for pheochromocytoma and hyperparathyroidism; offer family cascade testing
No inherited syndrome; RET still drives targeted therapy in advanced disease

bullets: Serum calcitonin and CEA (baseline and for a doubling-time later)
Germline RET testing in all; if positive, screen for pheochromocytoma (plasma / urine metanephrines) and hyperparathyroidism (calcium / PTH) BEFORE thyroid surgery
Neck ultrasound; cross-sectional imaging for high calcitonin (e.g. > 500 pg/mL) to detect distant metastases
Medullary carcinoma does not concentrate radioiodine and is not TSH-driven

nodes.name: MTC stage
nodes.title: Medullary: extent of disease
nodes.description: Choose an unaffected germline carrier, localized resectable disease, or advanced / distant metastatic medullary carcinoma.

options.label: Germline RET carrier, no cancer yet (prophylactic)

nodes.name: MEN2 prophylactic
nodes.title: Germline RET carrier: prophylactic thyroidectomy
nodes.description: Risk-reducing surgery in an unaffected MEN2 carrier, timed by the specific RET mutation's aggressiveness.
bullets: Timing is mutation-driven: earliest infancy for the highest-risk MEN2B (RET M918T), early childhood for high-risk, later and calcitonin-guided for moderate-risk mutations
Screen for and treat pheochromocytoma before any surgery
Total thyroidectomy; add central neck dissection if calcitonin is elevated or nodes look abnormal
Levothyroxine replacement afterward; begin lifelong calcitonin surveillance
Offer cascade genetic testing to at-risk relatives

nodes.name: MTC localized
nodes.title: Localized MTC: total thyroidectomy + central neck dissection
nodes.description: Surgery is the only curative modality for medullary carcinoma. Proceed to a calcitonin-based response assessment.
bullets: Total thyroidectomy with prophylactic central (level VI) neck dissection; add lateral dissection for imaging or biochemical evidence of nodal disease
Treat any pheochromocytoma FIRST if present (avoid intra-operative crisis)
Levothyroxine for replacement only - no TSH suppression, no radioiodine (C-cells are not iodine-avid or TSH-driven)
External-beam radiation for high-risk unresectable neck disease
Then assess the post-operative calcitonin response (next step)

nodes.name: MTC response
nodes.title: Medullary: post-operative biochemical response
nodes.description: Reassess calcitonin and CEA after surgery. An undetectable marker predicts cure; a persistent or rising marker with a short doubling-time drives restaging and systemic therapy.

options.label: Persistent / rising calcitonin, no structural disease

nodes.name: MTC restage
nodes.title: Medullary: restage structural disease
nodes.description: Structural medullary disease is present. Distinguish resectable neck disease from distant metastases, which decides reoperation versus systemic therapy.
bullets: Neck ultrasound and cross-sectional imaging (CT neck / chest / abdomen); consider DOTATATE or FDG-PET for occult disease
Resectable neck disease: compartment-oriented reoperation, then biochemical follow-up
Distant metastases: assess RET status and enter the advanced pathway

nodes.name: MTC RET status
nodes.title: Advanced MTC: RET status (first line)
nodes.description: In progressive advanced medullary carcinoma, a RET alteration selects a selective RET inhibitor over a multikinase inhibitor.

nodes.name: MTC RET+ 1L
nodes.title: Advanced MTC, RET-mutant: selpercatinib (first line)
nodes.description: RET-mutant advanced / progressive medullary carcinoma, first line.
bullets: Selpercatinib (or pralsetinib) - selective RET inhibitor, preferred first line for RET-mutant disease
Confirm the RET alteration on validated testing
Reserve for progressive or symptomatic disease; monitor LFTs, blood pressure, QT, and hypersensitivity
Trend calcitonin and CEA as response markers
Referenced dose protocol below; reassess at progression

nodes.name: MTC RET progression
nodes.title: RET-mutant MTC: on progression
nodes.description: Progression on a selective RET inhibitor. Distinguish oligoprogressive from systemic progression.

nodes.name: MTC RET+ 2L
nodes.title: RET-mutant MTC: multikinase inhibitor after a RET inhibitor
nodes.description: Systemic progression on a selective RET inhibitor.
bullets: Re-biopsy / plasma NGS for an acquired RET resistance mutation (e.g. solvent-front G810)
Cabozantinib or vandetanib multikinase inhibitor as the next line
A next-generation RET inhibitor on trial for an on-target solvent-front mutation where available
Directed local therapy and a bone-modifying agent for symptomatic or skeletal lesions
Referenced dose protocol below is the vandetanib multikinase-inhibitor option; enter medullary surveillance

nodes.name: MTC RET WT 1L
nodes.title: Advanced MTC, RET wild-type: multikinase inhibitor (first line)
nodes.description: Progressive advanced medullary carcinoma without a targetable RET alteration.
bullets: Cabozantinib or vandetanib (multikinase inhibitors) for progressive / symptomatic disease
Referenced dose protocol below is vandetanib (requires QT / ECG monitoring); cabozantinib is an alternative requiring wound / GI-perforation and hemorrhage vigilance
Observe indolent, asymptomatic metastatic disease with a calcitonin / CEA doubling-time
Directed local therapy and a bone-modifying agent for symptomatic or skeletal lesions
On progression: reassess for a next-line option

nodes.name: MTC MKI progression
nodes.title: RET wild-type MTC: on progression
nodes.description: Progression on a first multikinase inhibitor. Distinguish oligoprogressive from systemic progression.

nodes.name: MTC RET WT 2L
nodes.title: RET wild-type MTC: alternate multikinase inhibitor / trial
nodes.description: Systemic progression on a first multikinase inhibitor.
bullets: Switch to the alternate multikinase inhibitor (cabozantinib after vandetanib, or vice versa)
Re-send NGS to catch a late actionable driver (rare somatic RET, high TMB / MSI)
Clinical trial or best supportive care per performance status and goals
Referenced dose protocol below is the vandetanib multikinase-inhibitor option
Enter medullary surveillance

nodes.name: MTC surveillance
nodes.title: Medullary: surveillance
nodes.description: Biochemical follow-up after medullary carcinoma therapy; rising markers re-enter the advanced pathway.
bullets: Serial calcitonin and CEA; a short doubling-time (< 6-12 months) predicts progression and worse survival
Neck ultrasound and cross-sectional imaging guided by the calcitonin level and trend
Continue germline / familial screening and MEN2 comorbidity surveillance where relevant
Rising markers or new lesions: restage and enter the advanced medullary pathway

nodes.name: ATC workup
nodes.title: Anaplastic: emergent workup
nodes.description: Anaplastic carcinoma is rapidly lethal and an oncologic emergency. Move fast: airway, staging, and rapid mutation testing in parallel.
bullets: Airway assessment first: laryngoscopy; involve airway surgery early; tracheostomy only if truly needed
Rapid BRAF V600E testing (IHC and / or molecular) - expedite, it changes first-line therapy
Broader NGS (NTRK, RET, MMR / MSI, PD-L1) alongside BRAF
Whole-body staging (CT neck / chest / abdomen + brain imaging); essentially all are AJCC stage IV
Establish goals of care early given prognosis; multidisciplinary tumor board

nodes.name: ATC resectability
nodes.title: Anaplastic: resectability / extent (AJCC stage IV)
nodes.description: Anaplastic disease is stratified by resectability and distant spread, which sets the local-therapy plan.

tables.title: Anaplastic thyroid carcinoma - AJCC stage IV substages
rows: Gross extrathyroidal extension or nodal disease, often unresectable

nodes.name: ATC resectable
nodes.title: Resectable ATC: surgery + adjuvant chemoradiation
nodes.description: Complete resection followed by adjuvant therapy in the minority with resectable disease. Then reassess for adjuvant response.
bullets: Total thyroidectomy with therapeutic neck dissection when a complete (R0 / R1) resection is achievable without unacceptable morbidity
Adjuvant external-beam radiation, often concurrent with radiosensitizing chemotherapy (e.g. a taxane +/- platinum)
If BRAF V600E positive, neoadjuvant dabrafenib + trametinib may convert borderline disease to resectable - see the BRAF arm
No dedicated cytotoxic protocol here for this indication - shown as guidance
Then reassess local control / distant progression (next step)

nodes.name: ATC adjuvant response
nodes.title: Resected ATC: local control vs progression
nodes.description: After resection and adjuvant chemoradiation, reassess. Durable local control enters surveillance; new distant or unresectable progression enters the systemic BRAF-directed pathway.

nodes.name: ATC BRAF status
nodes.title: Unresectable ATC: BRAF V600E status (first line)
nodes.description: In unresectable / metastatic anaplastic disease, BRAF V600E status decides first-line systemic therapy.

nodes.name: ATC BRAF+ 1L
nodes.title: Unresectable ATC, BRAF V600E: dabrafenib + trametinib (first line)
nodes.description: BRAF V600E-mutant unresectable / metastatic anaplastic thyroid carcinoma, first line.
bullets: Dabrafenib + trametinib (BRAF + MEK inhibition) - rapid responses; start without delay
Consider adding an immune-checkpoint inhibitor, and reassess for surgery / radiation if a good response converts the tumor to resectable
Monitor fever (dabrafenib), skin, cardiac (LVEF), and ocular toxicity
Referenced dose protocol below; reassess at progression

nodes.name: ATC BRAF progression
nodes.title: BRAF V600E ATC: on progression
nodes.description: Progression on dabrafenib + trametinib. Distinguish limited disease amenable to continued therapy plus local measures from systemic progression needing a change.

options.label: Limited progression (add local therapy / checkpoint inhibitor, continue)

nodes.name: ATC BRAF+ 2L
nodes.title: BRAF V600E ATC: after BRAF-directed progression
nodes.description: Systemic progression on dabrafenib + trametinib.
bullets: Add or switch to an immune-checkpoint inhibitor (e.g. pembrolizumab) combined with continued BRAF / MEK blockade where feasible
Re-send NGS for a second actionable driver (NTRK, RET fusion, high TMB / MSI)
Cytotoxic chemotherapy (a taxane +/- platinum) or a clinical trial for fit patients; otherwise best supportive care
Referenced dose protocol below is the pembrolizumab checkpoint-inhibitor option
Continue palliative care and airway / symptom management

nodes.name: ATC BRAF-WT biomarker
nodes.title: Unresectable ATC, BRAF wild-type: actionable driver
nodes.description: BRAF wild-type anaplastic disease is driven by any other actionable alteration on NGS; otherwise it is managed with immunotherapy or cytotoxic chemoradiation, ideally on trial.

nodes.name: ATC NTRK
nodes.title: BRAF-WT ATC, NTRK fusion: TRK inhibitor
nodes.description: NTRK-fusion-positive anaplastic thyroid carcinoma.
bullets: Larotrectinib or entrectinib (tissue-agnostic TRK inhibitor indication) - can produce rapid responses even in anaplastic disease
Confirm the NTRK fusion on validated NGS; start without delay given prognosis
Referenced dose protocol below (larotrectinib; entrectinib is an alternative)
Continue multidisciplinary and palliative care; consider local therapy for airway control

nodes.name: ATC RET
nodes.title: BRAF-WT ATC, RET fusion: selective RET inhibitor
nodes.description: RET-fusion-positive anaplastic thyroid carcinoma.
bullets: Selpercatinib (or pralsetinib) - selective RET inhibitor for a confirmed RET fusion
Referenced dose protocol is the medullary-scoped selpercatinib protocol (same drug); the physician confirms the fit
Start without delay given prognosis; monitor LFTs, blood pressure, QT, and hypersensitivity
Continue multidisciplinary and palliative care; local therapy for airway control

nodes.name: ATC immunotherapy
nodes.title: BRAF-WT ATC, high TMB / MSI / PD-L1: immunotherapy
nodes.description: Anaplastic disease with a favorable immunotherapy biomarker.
bullets: An immune-checkpoint inhibitor (e.g. pembrolizumab), alone or added to cytotoxic chemoradiation, for high TMB / MSI-high / PD-L1-high disease
Enroll on a clinical trial where available
Referenced dose protocol below is pembrolizumab; monitor for immune-related adverse events
Continue multidisciplinary and palliative care; local therapy for airway control

nodes.name: ATC chemoradiation
nodes.title: BRAF-WT ATC, no target: chemoradiation / trial / supportive care
nodes.description: BRAF wild-type anaplastic disease without an actionable driver.
bullets: Clinical trial is strongly preferred where available
Cytotoxic chemoradiation (a taxane +/- platinum) for local control in fit patients
Best supportive care and early palliative care per goals when systemic therapy is not appropriate
Referenced dose protocol below is weekly paclitaxel + carboplatin (radiosensitizing) for fit patients
Airway and symptom management throughout

nodes.name: ATC surveillance
nodes.title: Anaplastic: short-interval monitoring
nodes.description: Close monitoring after anaplastic therapy; almost any new finding re-enters the systemic pathway.
bullets: Short-interval clinical review and cross-sectional imaging (including brain) given the aggressive course
Ongoing airway and symptom monitoring; maintain goals-of-care discussion
New distant or locoregional progression re-enters the BRAF / driver systemic pathway
Continue palliative and multidisciplinary care

nodes.name: Surveillance
nodes.title: Post-treatment surveillance
nodes.description: General follow-up entry for a previously treated patient; the cadence and markers depend on the original subtype.
bullets: Differentiated: thyroglobulin + antibody, neck ultrasound, dynamic response category; adjust the TSH target
Medullary: calcitonin and CEA with a doubling-time; imaging by level and trend
Anaplastic: short-interval clinical and cross-sectional imaging; symptom and airway monitoring
Any new biochemical or structural recurrence re-enters the matching subtype pathway
